what_it_is: Magnetic pulses to mood-related brain areas; non-invasive
patients: After 2+ failed antidepressants (insurer rule); overlaps with client's second-line patients
how_given: Clinic: 36 sessions over 6-9 weeks (SAINT: 50 sessions in 5 days, FDA-cleared 2022)
insurance: Usually covered after 2-4 failed antidepressants, with pre-approval; $500-3,000 out of pocket
threat_to_client: Medium: competes for patients failing pills, but needs daily clinic visits

what_it_is: Smartphone program: cognitive-emotional training + CBT lessons
patients: Adults with MDD on an antidepressant who responded only partly: the client's exact slot
how_given: Self-use at home: 18 sessions over 6 weeks, alongside an antidepressant
evidence: FDA-cleared Apr 2024 (Otsuka, Click Therapeutics), but trial did not beat a sham app significantly
threat_to_client: Low: weak evidence, uncertain coverage; more a complement than a substitute

what_it_is: Off-label IV ketamine (the drug is FDA-approved only as an anaesthetic)
how_given: Clinic: 4-6 infusions over ~2 weeks, then boosters
evidence: Fast effect; off-label, limited long-term data
threat_to_client: Low-medium: severe, cash-paying patients; one step beyond the client

what_it_is: Talk therapy with a trained therapist
patients: All severities; usually combined with medication
how_given: Weekly sessions, in person or online
evidence: Adding therapy to antidepressants improves outcomes vs pills alone (meta-analysis: g = 0.43, effect lasts up to 2 years)
threat_to_client: Low as a substitute: mostly used alongside pills, so a complement
